wikipedia_requests.title: Talk:Treatment of bipolar disorder
wikipedia_requests.section_title: Update Omega-3 fatty acids section with current evidence
wikipedia_requests.text:
{{edit COI}}
I am a co-author of the 2016 trial cited below, so I am requesting this change rather than editing the article directly.

'''Specific change:''' In § Omega-3 fatty acids, update the evidence summary to reflect current secondary literature. Suggested text:

Evidence for omega-3 fatty acids as an adjunctive treatment for bipolar disorder remains inconsistent. A 2019 systematic review of randomized placebo-controlled trials found some promising effects, particularly for depressive symptoms, but concluded that the overall evidence for adjunctive nutraceuticals in bipolar disorder was inconsistent.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Fusar-Poli L, Surace T, Vanella A, Meo V, Patania F, Furnari R, Signorelli MS, Aguglia E |title=The effect of adjunctive nutraceuticals in bipolar disorder: A systematic review of randomized placebo-controlled trials |journal=Journal of Affective Disorders |year=2019 |volume=252 |pages=334–349 |doi=10.1016/j.jad.2019.04.039 |pmid=30999090}}</ref> A 2025 review likewise described the clinical evidence as heterogeneous and conflicting. It included a 2016 double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 100 patients with bipolar I disorder that reported lower mania scores after adjunctive 1,000 mg/day omega-3 for three months; later higher-level evidence has not established a consistent benefit for mania.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Psara E, Papadopoulou SK, Mentzelou M, Voulgaridou G, Vorvolakos T, Apostolou T, Giaginis C |title=Omega-3 Fatty Acids for the Treatment of Bipolar Disorder Symptoms: A Narrative Review of the Current Clinical Evidence |journal=Marine Drugs |year=2025 |volume=23 |issue=2 |page=84 |doi=10.3390/md23020084 |pmid=39997208 |pmc=PMC11857698}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Shakeri J, Khanegi M, Golshani S, Farnia V, Tatari F, Alikhani M, Nooripour R, Ghezelbash MS |title=Effects of Omega-3 Supplement in the Treatment of Patients with Bipolar I Disorder |journal=International Journal of Preventive Medicine |year=2016 |volume=7 |page=77 |doi=10.4103/2008-7802.182734 |pmid=27280013 |pmc=PMC4882968}}</ref>

'''Reason:''' The section currently relies heavily on older evidence. The proposed change anchors the summary in 2019 and 2025 secondary sources while giving the 2016 primary trial only narrow, explicitly contextualized weight.

<!-- Ghezelbash-COI-Omega3-20260816 -->
~~~~

wikipedia_requests.title: Talk:Attachment and health
wikipedia_requests.section_title: Update Mental health section with recent meta-analytic evidence
wikipedia_requests.text:
{{edit COI}}
I am a co-author of the 2021 MDD study cited below, so I am requesting this change rather than editing the article directly.

'''Specific change:''' In § Mental health, add a brief update anchored in recent meta-analytic evidence:

More recent meta-analytic evidence supports a robust association between adult attachment insecurity and mental-health outcomes. A 2022 meta-analysis of 224 studies (245 samples; N=79,722) found moderate associations between attachment anxiety and avoidance and poorer mental health, including depression and anxiety.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Zhang X, Li J, Xie F, Chen X, Xu W, Hudson NW |title=The relationship between adult attachment and mental health: A meta-analysis |journal=Journal of Personality and Social Psychology |year=2022 |volume=123 |issue=5 |pages=1089–1137 |doi=10.1037/pspp0000437 |pmid=36201836}}</ref> Consistent with this broader literature, a 2021 cross-sectional study of 300 people with major depressive disorder reported high rates of insecure attachment and an association between anxious attachment and dissociative symptoms; because the study was cross-sectional, it does not establish causality.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Golshani S, Najafpour A, Hashemian SS, Goudarzi N, Firoozabadi A, Ghezelbash MS, Hookari S, Firoozabadi K, Dürsteler KM, Brühl AB, Alikhani M, Sadeghi-Bahmani D, Brand S |title=Individuals with Major Depressive Disorder Report High Scores of Insecure-Avoidant and Insecure-Anxious Attachment Styles, Dissociative Identity Symptoms, and Adult Traumatic Events |journal=Healthcare |year=2021 |volume=9 |issue=9 |page=1169 |doi=10.3390/healthcare9091169 |pmid=34574943 |pmc=PMC8469763}}</ref>

'''Reason:''' The existing section relies mainly on older literature. This proposal anchors the general claim in a large recent meta-analysis and uses the 2021 study only as a narrowly framed clinical example with its design limitation stated explicitly.

<!-- Ghezelbash-COI-Attachment-20260816 -->
~~~~
